outcome.answer:
I'll search the knowledge graph for your house rule on yield reporting.Good hit. Let me read the full playbook note on yield reporting:**Yes, there's a house rule: state the purification step with the yield.**

[[playbook-recrystallisation-purity]]

The key principle is that **an 88% yield after recrystallisation and an 88% yield after a plug are not the same number**. The purification method drastically changes what the yield means for a scale-up — if you're planning to repeat a route and the original hit an 88% after a simple chromatography plug but you measured it as 88% after a slow recrystallisation, your scale-up target becomes unreachable.

**Every reaction note in the corpus pairs the yield with its purification step.** So when you write it up, include both: e.g. "88% yield (after recrystallisation)" or "76% yield (chromatography)".

This is sourced from [[campaign-aspirin-teaching]], which distilled this rule from actual scale-up mismatches.
